money-and-cost.cash_card_notes: Iceland's currency is the Icelandic Kroner (ISK). Declare cash of over 10,000 euros or equivalent if you're travelling between Iceland and any non-EU country. This covers all forms of currency, not only cash. You'll have to pay a fine on entry or exit if you: don't declare your money give incorrect information You can use major credit cards in most places.

laws.rule: Penalties for drug offences, even for possession of small amounts of recreational drugs or some prescription medications, include: heavy fines imprisonment being removed from the Schengen area a potential entry ban If you intend to take medication, confirm it's legal in your destination. Check if any rules or restrictions apply. Depending on your medication, you may need to apply for a permit to bring it to your destination. Always carry a copy of your prescription and transport your medication in its original container.
laws.heading: Drugs

laws.rule: Always carry an ID, such as your driver's licence or a copy of your passport. Penalties for drink driving and speeding are severe and include the following: heavy fines jail sentences Even minor offences can attract fines and jail sentences. If you're found guilty of an offence: you may face jail or deportation you may be banned from the Schengen area
laws.heading: Other laws

laws.rule: Australian driving licences are valid in Iceland if you have had your licence for a minimum of 1 year. However, some car rental companies require customers to present an International Driving Permit (IDP) if holding a licence issued outside Europe or North America. Digital driver's licences may not be accepted. If you need an IDP, get this before you leave Australia. An IDP doesn't replace the requirement for a regular driver's license. laws.heading: Driving permit

laws.rule: Drones are generally limited to 120 m above ground and to visual line of sight. Operators, including visitors from outside the EU, register on flydrone.is, and drones over 250 g need the A1/A3 test. Near volcanic eruptions the Transport Authority has set separate prohibited areas, so check its notices before flying.
laws.heading: Drone rules

laws.rule: Off-road driving in the highlands is prohibited. The Icelandic Road and Coastal Administration says unauthorised off-road driving carries prosecution, substantial fines or imprisonment under the Nature Conservation Act No. 60/2013. Mountain roads (F-roads) are usually rough, steep or have unbridged river crossings, are open only part of the year (some, such as Sprengisandur, not fully open until early July), and the Administration asks travellers not to enter the highlands off-season without permission. Landmannalaugar and the Diamond Circle were not checked.
laws.penalty_signal: prosecution, fines or imprisonment; amounts not stated on the page

laws.rule: Under Article 75 of the Schengen Convention, a traveller carrying narcotic drugs or psychotropic substances for their own medical treatment must be able to produce, at a check, a certificate issued or authenticated by a competent authority of their state of residence. The certificate form covers the substance, quantity and length of the journey. How a resident of Australia obtains one is not checked in this entry; ask this country's embassy or health authority before travel.

visa-preparation.fastest_entry: Visa-free short stays (90 days or less) as part of the Schengen area, in some cases.
visa-preparation.before_departure: Nothing to lodge before travel today: EES registration happens at the border. ETIAS hadn't started on 2026-11-01.
steps: Iceland is in the Schengen area: short stays of 90 days or less can be visa-free in some cases; other purposes or longer stays need a visa before travel.
At the first Schengen border, give fingerprints and a photo for the Entry/Exit System (EES). It's free; nothing is needed before arrival, and sites charging for it are fraudulent.
Carry your passport when crossing borders, including inside Schengen (temporary internal checks are in place in places).

drone-pilot-pathway.summary: Iceland applies the EU drone rules through the Icelandic Transport Authority: operators register on flydrone.is and drones over 250 g need the A1/A3 online test. No public operator directory found; what a visitor flying for work must do was not spelled out.

items.text: Not yet checked: no public Transport Authority directory of drone operators was found on the pages read.

Operators register on flydrone.is (registration lasts five years). Drones over 250 g need a pass in the A1/A3 test; the A2 exam is taken at the Transport Authority or an approved institution. The Authority says commercial drones face additional requirements, without spelling them out on the pages read.

Not yet checked: how a visitor operating commercially registers and what authorisation applies. The Authority's guidance says operators from outside the EU register on flydrone.is; flydrone@samgongustofa.is is the contact it gives.
